Name: 7-Zip
Description: The vendor's NSIS installer, wrapped so Intune gets a ProductCode to detect on and a real uninstall.
Awkwardness: Wrapping an EXE installer inside an MSI splits ownership of the files: Windows Installer knows about the wrapper, and the vendor installer owns everything it laid down. Uninstalling the MSI therefore removes nothing unless the package explicitly calls the vendor's own Uninstall.exe, and a failed install leaves 7-Zip behind unless the same command is registered as a rollback. There is also an NSIS trap in the switches - /D= must be the last argument and must not be quoted, even when the path contains spaces - so the natural-looking /D="C:\Program Files\7-Zip" is ignored and the install lands in the default location instead.
DownloadNotes: Take the .exe installer for the architecture you are deploying, not the .msi - a Windows Installer package cannot be nested inside another one.
Notes: Set Version to the 7-Zip version you downloaded before building.
Verified in this repository: built, installed, upgraded and uninstalled under msiexec.
The payload is copied into the package as setup.exe whatever you called it, so a new 7-Zip release does not change the project beyond its Version.

Uninstall is the vendor's own Uninstall.exe, addressed by absolute path because it is not part of the payload. It is also registered as the install action's rollback, so a package that fails later does not leave 7-Zip installed.
The uninstall action ignores its exit code: someone removing 7-Zip by hand first should not make the MSI uninstall fail.
Change the /D= path and the two Uninstall.exe paths together, or the uninstall will look in the wrong place.

Arp.Comments: 7-Zip's vendor installer wrapped as an MSI, with the vendor uninstaller wired to uninstall and to rollback.
